audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Chronicles / Divrei Hayamim Aleph priestly and Levitical divisions, first-pass restored draft; later witness audit required
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Nadab and Abihu, hereditary priesthood, proportional divisions, lots, scribal transparency, old/young equality, and textual variants.

verses.restored: Divisions of sons of Aaron: sons of Aaron were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
Nadab and Abihu died before their father and had no children; Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests.
David, with Zadok from sons of Eleazar and Ahimelech from sons of Ithamar, divided them according to appointed service.
More chief men were found among sons of Eleazar than sons of Ithamar, so they divided them: sixteen ancestral heads from Eleazar and eight from Ithamar.
They divided them by lot, these with those, because officials of sanctuary and officials of Divine house came from both Eleazar and Ithamar.

Shemaiah son of Nethanel, Levite scribe, wrote them before king, leaders, Zadok the priest, Ahimelech son of Abiathar, and ancestral heads of priests and Levites, one ancestral house drawn for Eleazar and then one for Ithamar.
First lot came to Jehoiarib, second to Jedaiah,
third to Harim, fourth to Seorim,
fifth to Malchijah, sixth to Mijamin,
seventh to Hakkoz, eighth to Abijah,
ninth to Jeshua, tenth to Shecaniah,
eleventh to Eliashib, twelfth to Jakim,
thirteenth to Huppah, fourteenth to Jeshebeab,
fifteenth to Bilgah, sixteenth to Immer,
seventeenth to Hezir, eighteenth to Happizzez,
nineteenth to Pethahiah, twentieth to Jehezkel,
twenty-first to Jachin, twenty-second to Gamul,
twenty-third to Delaiah, twenty-fourth to Maaziah.
These were appointments for service, to enter house of YHWH according to ordinance through Aaron their ancestor, as YHWH Divine of Israel commanded him.
Remaining descendants of Levi: from sons of Amram, Shubael; from sons of Shubael, Jehdeiah.
From Rehabiah, Isshiah the chief.
From Izharites, Shelomoth; from sons of Shelomoth, Jahath.
Sons of Hebron: Jeriah first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, Jekameam fourth.
Son of Uzziel: Micah; from sons of Micah, Shamir.
Brother of Micah was Isshiah; from sons of Isshiah, Zechariah.
Sons of Merari: Mahli and Mushi; sons of Jaaziah: Beno.
Sons of Merari through Jaaziah: Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.
From Mahli: Eleazar, who had no sons.
From Kish: Jerahmeel his son.
Sons of Mushi: Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. These were Levite descendants by ancestral houses.
They also cast lots corresponding to relatives sons of Aaron before David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and ancestral heads of priests and Levites; chief ancestral house was treated like younger relative.

translation_notes: Nadab and Abihu's death belongs to a sacred-violence tradition and must not be used to terrorize religious workers or children.
Hereditary priesthood describes an ancient system and does not authorize modern caste, nepotism, or male-only spiritual authority.
Lots distribute work; they are not magical guarantees of Divine approval and require transparent, revisable administration.
Shemaiah's written record before multiple witnesses is a constructive accountability practice.
Equal treatment of chief and younger households limits seniority privilege, though labor consent and conditions remain unstated.
Childlessness is recorded administratively and does not diminish a person's worth.
Names and family relationships contain textual variants requiring witness audit.
safety_note: Do not use priestly divisions to justify clerical caste, fear-based ritual control, nepotism, male supremacy, or divination by lots. Preserve transparent records, equal dignity, accountability, and safe working conditions.
